inventory.queue: JobQueue.submit(name,peakBytes) reserves original position; cycle reconciles native outcomes then applies at most one policy control; allocationBlocked(name,attemptSequence,waitSequence) accepts current denial; completedAttempts retains typed native payload. Attempt.start/resume/terminate/poll/close are the supported lifecycle; ordinary nonzero natural results are completions, not retry candidates. Aborted attempts preserve original action position and obey retry admission/completion thresholds. No native launch/adoption implementation is supplied by this interface.

supported_Cargo_sequences.sequence: Cargo job_queue permits active jobs < explicit acquired tokens +1, then starts rustc/build-script job. ProcessBuilder.inherit_jobserver passes the selected client to both compiler and script commands. Wrapper already occupies the Cargo-granted outer slot; it does not acquire another token merely to launch one compiler. Keep wrapper alive across admitted targeted retries and return exactly one final status to Cargo. Inner rustc/make threads borrow extra tokens from the same pool.

Cargo fingerprint/dependency scheduling decides freshness before execution. scope_cases.linker: The linker remains a descendant in its parent rustc action, sharing admission estimate, whole-tree measurement, cancellation, result and Cargo outer slot. Do not submit a separate queue action that double-counts its parent. Install/reinstall allocation hooks before each linker/exec image release; a rustc-only hook does not cover linker allocation. Native descendant exec/fork and containment proof is a required gate.
scope_cases.build_script: Compiling build.rs belongs to a compiler attempt. Executing the resulting build script is a distinct Cargo action, with any C/C++ compiler/linker children inside that script attempt. No stable1.95 build-script CLI wrapper was found in the actual direct execution path; full coverage needs a verified native held-child registration/adoption operation or another demonstrated existing mechanism before implementation. Replacing built executables with shims or patching Cargo is not selected.
scope_cases.cache_hits: Cargo fresh units produce no compiler action. A preexisting caching wrapper may answer without spawning rustc; preserve that hit path and submit expensive child only if it exists. Placing memory admission outside a cache wrapper would unnecessarily gate hits and changes the claimed action; exact ordering and hit/no-rustc receipts are required. No existing sccache workflow configuration was found in the bounded .github/tooling scan; caller-supplied wrappers remain a contract to preserve.
scope_cases.nested_Cargo: A nested Cargo launched synchronously by a build script inherits its existing outer slot plus shared explicit client; never create a second pool or implicit root slot for it. Passing copied MAKEFLAGS alone does not authorize an additional token. If parent script waits for nested actions, charging parent as an active memory action while denying every child can deadlock a one-slot admission policy. The controller needs a verified retained-parent/delegated-capacity relationship or must retain the entire nested subtree inside the script attempt. Exact classification and child-action delegation are unproved; fail explicitly rather than silently treating nested Cargo as a new root.
scope_cases.token_loss: Persistent wrapper retains Cargo outer slot when a compiler subprocess retries. It does not guarantee return of extra tokens borrowed internally by killed rustc/linker/make. Native Windows proof explicitly demonstrates acquired-token loss after forced death. Quiescent observed deficit must remain failure; no owner reseeding. Prefer in-process allocation resume; arbitrary killed consumers cannot be accepted as safe retry from current evidence.
